statement: ECF is declared to be only an encoding of EAM; the Index is deliberately excluded from the authoritative section set so a reader may discard and rebuild it.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §4.5 L425 / I10 (Index reconstructible); consistent with docs/format-v0.md §Index handling L465-475

statement: Public ECF surface re-exports INDEXED encode/open/verify families with policy/limit variants, peek_layout, the INDEXED random-access reader (open_indexed_random), STREAM encode/open/verify families, StagingLimits and sequential limit constructors.
The 8-byte magic 8E 45 42 31 0D 0A 1A 0A is labelled only a 'Candidate' magic selected by the architecture specification; the code does not treat it as frozen.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §18.3 L2066, L2073 (magic not frozen until identification-database collision check); docs/format-v0.md §Container L48
evidence_in_source: code comment 'Candidate'; unit test ecf.rs::bootstrap_capabilities_are_complete_and_indexed asserts bytes (L271-278)
research_needed: Collision check against libmagic, shared-mime-info, PRONOM and TrID databases; semantics of the generation digit '1'.
decision_needed: Is 8E 'EB1' CR LF 1A LF the frozen v1 magic, and when does the generation digit change?

statement: Fixed physical widths: preamble 256 bytes, footer 128 bytes, section header 64 bytes, plan-driven Chunk frame header 64 bytes, extended (group_ref-carrying) Chunk frame header 96 bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches docs/format-v0.md §Exact bootstrap framing L222-297
evidence_in_source: code; native_ecf.rs imports FOOTER_LEN/PREAMBLE_LEN/SECTION_HEADER_LEN for corpus mutation
research_needed: Measure fixed overhead (448 bytes + 64 per section + 64/96 per chunk + 100 per Index entry) on small-file and many-chunk corpora versus tar/zip/7z.

statement: Incompat feature bits: 0x1 cross-file-compression-v1 (Dictionary/ChunkGroup sections, v2 frames), 0x2 codec-transform-v1 (TransformSteps, v4 registry), 0x4 reconstructive-transform-v1 (TransformStep v2, ReconstructionData), 0x8 whole-object-reconstruction-v1 (regions, v3 steps).
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md §Exact bootstrap framing L251-271

statement: stream-layout-v1 is required incompat bit 0x10; a reader not implementing it must refuse the archive rather than interpret the STREAM body as INDEXED sections.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.1 L2173 (unknown incompat MUST refuse)

statement: Further incompat bits: 0x2000 conversion-provenance-v1 (in-band type-28 record), 0x4000 legacy-preservation-v1 (exact legacy source plus LOM evidence), 0x8000 posix-metadata-v1 (Entry-v2), 0x10000 platform-security-metadata-v1 (Entry-v3). Bits 0x20-0x1000 are allocated to crypto (crypto/mod.rs:49-57).
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L255-258 lists the same recognised bits

statement: SUPPORTED_INCOMPAT_FEATURES is the union of the nine ECF bits and CRYPTO_FEATURES; any other incompat bit is refused at write (container.rs:1160-1166, 1303-1312) and at read (container.rs:2736-2745).

read_only_compat and compat bitmaps are written, checksummed and parsed but never interpreted: no bits are registered, unknown ro_compat/compat bits are silently accepted, and no operation (repack, recipient mutation, re-sign) is gated on them.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.10 L485 and §20.1 L2174-2175 (ro_compat MAY read, MUST NOT write; compat ignorable)
evidence_in_source: code; grep shows no consumer beyond inspection output (archive/tooling.rs:1311-1318)
research_needed: Design review of three-tier evolution against immutable-archive operations; conformance cases with unknown ro_compat/compat bits.
decision_needed: What operations count as 'writing' for ro_compat (repack, key add/remove, signature add), and must current tools refuse unknown ro_compat bits before rewriting?

statement: The only format namespace is 'ecf/bootstrap-v1', documented in code as the versioned namespace for the experimental encoding; no frozen v1 namespace exists.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L3-4 (experimental implementation note, not a frozen v1 specification)
decision_needed: When and under what name does the bootstrap namespace become the frozen Entrybound v1 wire namespace, and are bootstrap archives accepted afterwards?

statement: Crate-private helpers compute exact encoded lengths of TransformPlan (v1/v2/v3), ReconstructionRegion, ReconstructionData, Dictionary, ChunkGroup and legacy evidence records; the planner (planner.rs:27-28, 514-523, 1679-1687) and ZIP import (legacy/zip.rs:2607) use them for container cost accounting.
research_needed: Harness access requires a research feature flag (items are pub(crate)).

statement: Only FormatVersion 0.1 (BOOTSTRAP, 'supported experimental format version') exists; the reader refuses every other major/minor pair with UnsupportedVersion, including unknown minor versions.
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows SPEC §4.2 L375 (reader rejects unknown major version immediately); minor-version tolerance unspecified in code
decision_needed: What are v1 major/minor semantics relative to feature bits and namespace, and should an unknown minor version be readable?

statement: SectionKind enumerates Descriptor, TransformPlans, Dictionaries, ChunkGroups, ReconstructionData, ReconstructionRegions, ChunkData, ManifestRecords, Fidelity and the non-authoritative Index, described as 'justified by the first native vertical slice'.
refines_or_supersedes: Differs from SPEC §4.3 L409 section list (METADATA, CRYPTO_ENVELOPE, SIGNATURES, CONVERSION_RECORD, MERKLE_OUTBOARD absent; Reconstruction sections added)

statement: No SIGNATURES, CONVERSION_RECORD, METADATA or MERKLE_OUTBOARD section exists in unencrypted INDEXED; conversion and preservation records ride inside the FIDELITY payload and no outboard Merkle structure is serialized.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.3 L409 section types; SPEC §8.6 L975-977 MERKLE_OUTBOARD; CLI states unencrypted ECF has no normative embedded-signature placement (entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:4784)
research_needed: Cost/benefit of outboard Merkle for verified partial reads versus flat chunk digests; remote-read round-trip measurements.
decision_needed: Does v1 need a MERKLE_OUTBOARD and SIGNATURES section for unencrypted archives, or are per-chunk digests plus detached .ebsig sufficient?

statement: BootstrapCapabilities (version, layout, role, budget_declared; default INDEXED/Complete/true) is public but referenced only by its own unit test; no writer or reader consumes it.
evidence_in_source: code; grep shows use only in ecf.rs tests (L266-278)
decision_needed: Remove BootstrapCapabilities or make it the writer's declared-capability input?

statement: Section magic is 'EBS1', Chunk frame magic 'EBCH', footer magic 8E 'EBF' CR LF 1A LF, and every section header version is 1.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L240-243, L276, L290

statement: WriteOptions for INDEXED has a single field include_index (default true); it affects only reconstructible physical data, so no other writer knob (section alignment, padding, ordering) exists.
IndexStatus has four outcomes: PresentValid, RebuiltAbsent, RebuiltInvalid and NotApplicableStream (STREAM has no Index by design).
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md §Index handling L467-475

statement: VerificationReport lists fifteen checked guarantees plus Index status/reason and identities, but every boolean is hard-set true on success; any failed check aborts with Err, so the report never expresses partially verified or unchecked states.
decision_needed: Should verification reports carry per-check tri-state (passed/failed/not-checked) for partial or remote verification?

statement: INDEXED open/verify is strictly fail-fast: the first diagnostic aborts, with no continue-on-error mode, no multi-error collection, no per-entry salvage and no localisation beyond the first failing section or Chunk.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with SPEC §11.4 L1386 (strict parsing, recovery is separate salvage operation); salvage not in this slice
research_needed: Blast-radius measurement: flip bytes across regions and record how much content remains recoverable by a salvage tool.
decision_needed: Is a separate salvage reader required for v1, and what localisation must verify report?

statement: The INDEXED writer validates the EAM, the TransformPlan registry and the feature model, and recomputes native identities before any serialisation.
Every incompat bit required by a TransformPlan (codec::required_features) must be declared in the archive's incompat bitmap; otherwise encoding fails Unsupported/UnsupportedRequiredFeature.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.1 L2192 (unknown codec is incompat, fails closed at open)

statement: TransformPlan record schema is selected by features: TransformStep v3 items with whole-object 0x8, v2 with reconstructive 0x4, otherwise v1 steps if codec-transform 0x2 or a mandatory empty step sequence.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L347-362

statement: Unencrypted writers hardcode Descriptor identity_profile 1 (identity/v1) and digest_algorithm 1 (SHA-256) and always emit Descriptor record version 1 with no declarations; encrypted writers emit version 2.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md §Digests L205-212 (tree-native digest deferred to a future version) and L453-460 (unencrypted writers byte-frozen on Descriptor v1)
decision_needed: Is SHA-256 the sole v1 digest and identity/v1 the sole profile, or must v1 readers accept identity/strict-v1 and another digest id?

statement: ConversionProvenance (type 28) and LegacyPreservation (type 30) records are appended after the Fidelity record inside the FIDELITY section payload rather than occupying dedicated sections.
refines_or_supersedes: Differs from SPEC §4.3 L409 CONVERSION_RECORD section type

statement: Canonical INDEXED section order: base 1 Descriptor, 2 TransformPlans, 3 ChunkData, 4 Manifest, 5 Fidelity, 6 Index; 0x1 inserts Dictionaries(3), ChunkGroups(4); 0x4 adds ReconstructionData; 0x8 adds ReconstructionRegions before ChunkData; Index always last and optional.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches docs/format-v0.md L245-271

statement: Section numbering is a closed per-feature-combination table for (none), (0x1), (0x1+0x4) and (0x1+0x4+0x8); there is no section registry, no skippable/optional unknown section type, and an unknown id is refused Unsupported.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.3 L411 (INDEX is the only ignorable section)
research_needed: Extensibility review: impact of renumbering on independent readers and future features.
decision_needed: Will v1 keep feature-dependent renumbering of section ids, or assign stable global section type ids with an ignorable class for compat features?

statement: The optional INDEX section is appended after FIDELITY and stores absolute frame offsets computed as preamble length + CHUNK_DATA section offset + section header + relative frame offset.

Writer emits the footer with total length, Descriptor and Manifest locators, entry count, total logical size and SHA-256 of the preamble, then checks that the assembled container length equals the declared total.
PCI is SHA-256 over every exact container byte, computed after writing or on open and never embedded in the archive.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L217-218, L406-407
evidence_in_source: code; native_ecf.rs index test asserts PCI differs with Index (L239)

statement: The INDEXED writer materialises the entire container in memory (body Vec, then a second Vec of total length) from an Archive already holding every Chunk plaintext; there is no streaming or bounded-memory INDEXED writer.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §13.2 L1520 (no whole-file buffering)
research_needed: Measure peak RSS of pack/encode versus logical archive size; design a spill-to-file INDEXED writer.
decision_needed: Must the v1 INDEXED writer operate in bounded memory for archives larger than RAM?

statement: In-memory INDEXED open/verify require the whole container as &[u8] and decode every Chunk plaintext into the returned Archive, so memory scales with logical size up to caller budget (default 64 GiB); range-based reading exists separately in ecf/random.rs.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §13.2 L1520-1521 (no whole-file buffering, bounded memory)
research_needed: RSS of open/verify versus archive size; compare with ecf/random.rs range reader.
decision_needed: Should full verify use a streaming, plaintext-discarding path for INDEXED archives?

statement: verify, verify_with_policy and verify_with_limits are thin wrappers that run the complete open (all decoding and identity recomputation) and discard the archive; there is no cheaper structural-only verify level.
evidence_in_source: code; native_ecf.rs corpus uses verify for invalid Index (L406-409)
decision_needed: Does v1 need graded verify levels (structure, digests-without-decode, full)?

statement: Encrypted INDEXED writing reuses the same canonical record and Chunk-frame encoders; crypto framing changes only visibility and physical organisation, not EAM facts.

Crypto-v1 refuses archives carrying ConversionProvenance ('does not yet carry conversion provenance'); converted archives must stay unencrypted ECF. crypto/container.rs:1071-1072 also refuses conversion and preservation feature bits.
decision_needed: Must v1 support encrypting converted/preserved legacy archives, and where do private conversion records live?

statement: Production encrypted writers always prepare Descriptor v2; the pre-correction Descriptor v1 encrypted form is reproducible only under cfg(test) for compatibility fixtures.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L453-463 (Descriptor v2 correction; legacy v1 encrypted archives are labelled compatibility input)

statement: For encryption, CHUNK_DATA is split into one byte vector per Chunk frame and each authoritative section payload into one vector per canonical record, fixing the plaintext granularity crypto segments see.
research_needed: Measure ciphertext size and record-count leakage per granularity with padding enabled.

statement: After authentication the crypto reader rebuilds a temporary unencrypted INDEXED container in memory from the authenticated records and re-enters the ordinary reader, avoiding a second EAM parser.
research_needed: Peak memory of encrypted open (ciphertext + plaintext parts + temporary container + decoded chunks).

statement: The authenticated Descriptor record version (1 or 2) must equal the version selected by the crypto dispatch; disagreement is NoncanonicalEncoding.
Both readers require Descriptor namespace 'ecf/bootstrap-v1', identity_profile 1 and digest_algorithm 1; anything else is Unsupported/UnsupportedRequiredFeature.

Encrypted Descriptor v2 declarations are checked against caller budget and decode policy, and the declared DecodeRequirements must exactly equal those aggregated from authenticated plans, dictionaries and groups (else Corrupt/ResourceLimit).

For pre-correction encrypted Descriptor-v1 archives the reader parses with the caller policy (KDF cost forced 0) as provisional budget, then enforces the exact derived budget and reports budget_declared=false.
Encrypted open reports the PCI of the encrypted bytes, overriding the PCI of the temporary plaintext container.

FIDELITY payload holds exactly one Fidelity record; conversion-provenance-v1 requires exactly one following type-28 record; legacy-preservation-v1 requires conversion provenance plus one type-30 record; any undeclared trailing record is NoncanonicalEncoding.
evidence_in_source: code; legacy/zip.rs unit tests L3527-3543, L4395 (feature/record mismatch)

statement: open() and verify() apply bootstrap_resource_policy (1M entries, 64 GiB logical, 16 GiB single entry, 64000x expansion, 4M chunks, depth 1024, 1 GiB metadata, zero KDF cost) and decode policy (8 MiB window, 384 MiB working set), described as deliberately generous experimental limits.
refines_or_supersedes: archive.rs:32-59 (limits documented as experimental CLI defaults)
evidence_in_source: code; numbers chosen without cited measurement
research_needed: Corpus survey of real archive sizes/entry counts plus threat-model analysis of decompression-bomb and allocation limits to set v1 defaults.
decision_needed: What are the normative v1 default caller policies for open/verify/unpack?

statement: The INDEXED reader refuses a preamble declaring STREAM layout with Unsupported/UnsupportedRequiredFeature, directing the caller to the sequential reader.
Caller resource policy and decoder policy are enforced against the preamble declarations before the footer, sections or any payload are decoded.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.8 L472 (decide from preamble before allocation)

statement: In canonical INDEXED the preamble footer-offset hint must equal the actual fixed footer offset; a stale or zero hint is NoncanonicalEncoding although the footer is self-locating.
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows SPEC §4.2 L385 (footer locator hint advisory only, must not be trusted) and docs/format-v0.md L236
evidence_in_source: code only; no test found by grep of crates/*/tests
decision_needed: Is a mismatched advisory footer hint a conformance failure or ignorable, given the spec calls it advisory?

statement: All required sections for the declared feature schema must be present, and the footer's Descriptor and Manifest locators must equal the scanned section framing, else Corrupt/SectionStructure.
Descriptor v2 is private to corrected encrypted INDEXED archives: an unencrypted container with v2, or a corrected encrypted container with v1, is NoncanonicalEncoding.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L453-460

statement: The reader takes budget and decode declarations from the preamble unless Descriptor v2 supplies them, and hardcodes layout INDEXED, role Complete, dedup window 0, identity/v1 and SHA-256 into the decoded descriptor.

After decoding, EAM invariants are validated; footer entry count and total logical bytes must match records; derived actuals must not exceed any declared budget field; declared DecodeRequirements must equal the aggregate exactly (else Corrupt/ResourceLimit).
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.2 L391 (preamble bounds vs footer actuals)

statement: The reader recomputes every Entry identity and auxiliary digest plus LAI, PCR and AUX and fails with EntryIdentityMismatch, EntryAuxMismatch, LaiMismatch, PcrMismatch or AuxMismatch on disagreement with stored values.
Consumers must choose the reader from the archive's declared preamble layout (peek_layout reads only the preamble), never from whether the received source happens to be seekable.
evidence_in_source: code doc comment; no direct test of peek_layout found (CLI test a_stream_archive_in_a_file_is_never_reported_as_random_access covers behaviour)

statement: Caller-policy enforcement refuses (PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit) when any of the eight declared ResourceBudget fields exceeds the caller's corresponding limit.
Decoder-policy enforcement refuses when declared window or working-set bytes exceed policy or when any declared decode flag bit is not permitted by policy flags.
Crypto incompatibility bits are not part of an unencrypted EAM declaration; encode refuses them as Nonconforming.
stream-layout-v1 must be declared exactly when layout is STREAM, enforced at write (Nonconforming) and at preamble read.
Feature dependencies: whole-object-reconstruction-v1 requires cross-file, codec-transform and reconstructive bits; reconstructive-transform-v1 requires cross-file and codec-transform bits.
ReconstructionData/ReconstructionFallback objects require bit 0x4, and ReconstructionRegion/audit records require bit 0x8; otherwise Unsupported.
Every Dictionary is registry-validated; any Dictionary, ChunkGroup, Chunk group_ref or non-independent TransformPlan requires cross-file-compression-v1.

Without cross-file-compression-v1, INDEXED Chunk frames must be in ascending digest order ('historical'); with it, frame order follows the planner's physical_order and is authoritative for preceding-Chunk dependencies.
refines_or_supersedes: Refines docs/format-v0.md L273 ('digest-ordered frames') per L283

statement: validate_feature_model does not check posix-metadata, platform-security, conversion or preservation bits; those gates live in Archive::validate (eam/validate.rs:112-135), which both writers call first.

Descriptor normalisation forces format 0.1, namespace, role Complete, identity/v1, SHA-256 and a recomputed aggregate DecodeRequirements; INDEXED declares budget_declared=true and dedup window 0, overwriting caller-supplied values.
Descriptor planner_id and chunker_id must be non-empty strings; they are otherwise free-form (no registry check in the container).
decision_needed: Should planner_id/chunker_id values be registry-controlled or length-bounded in v1?

statement: A producer that declares no pre-payload budget (STREAM without budget) writes an all-zero ResourceBudget, and the reader bounds the pass with its own policy instead.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.2 L381, L393 (BudgetDeclared flag for unseekable producers)

statement: Derived budget is exact actuals: entry count, total logical bytes, largest ContentObject logical size, max expansion ratio, unique Chunk count, deepest path, metadata bound, and key-derivation cost fixed at 0.

max_metadata_bytes sums encoded manifest, ConversionProvenance, LegacyPreservation (including embedded full legacy source bytes), ReconstructionData and ReconstructionRegion representations, so payload-like bytes count against the metadata budget (default cap 1 GiB).
research_needed: Measure metadata-budget values for preservation and JPEG-region archives against default policy; check for false refusals.
decision_needed: Should preserved source bytes and region representations have their own budget field instead of max_metadata_bytes?

statement: Expansion ratio is ceil(logical*1000/stored) in milli-units with a floor of 1000; empty Chunks with empty storage count 0; region-owned Chunks are excluded and each region contributes logical_bytes over representation length; non-empty zero-stored Chunk is structural corruption.

INDEXED and STREAM share one Chunk frame encoder, one header parser and one payload decoder, so a frame's stored bytes and interpretation are identical across layouts; callers must present Chunks in physical_order.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md §Layout equivalence L409-416

statement: Chunk frame: 'EBCH', version u16 (1 base, 2 cross-file, 3 whole-object), flags u16, stored_len u64, chunk_id 32 bytes, logical_len u64, plan_ref u64, then group_ref 32 bytes (zero means none) for versions 2/3, then stored bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L273-288

statement: Frame flags must be zero except v3 flag value 1 (region-owned); a region-owned frame must have stored_len 0, plan_ref REGION_MEMBER_PLAN_REF (0) and no group, and the writer rejects conflicting ownership (InvalidReconstructionRegion).

Stored payload encoding dispatches by plan mode: Independent (plain or reconstruction-based), Dictionary (needs registered Dictionary), Prefix{lookback} (needs group_ref and ChunkGroup with equal lookback, else LookbackViolation); incompatible plan/group combinations are InvalidGroupReference.

Before decoding, each frame header is bounded: logical_len must not exceed declared max_single_entry_logical_bytes and (non-region) expansion ratio must not exceed declared max_expansion_ratio_milli, else Corrupt/ResourceLimit.
Chunk frame identities in CHUNK_DATA must be unique (exact deduplication: one frame per Chunk digest).
Every non-region-owned frame must reference a declared TransformPlan; an unknown plan_ref is Unsupported/UnknownTransformPlan.
The number of decoded Chunk frames must never exceed the declared chunk_count; the check runs incrementally while scanning CHUNK_DATA.

Each decoded plaintext's SHA-256 must equal its chunk_id; mismatch is ReconstructedDigestMismatch for reconstruction plans, PrerequisiteChunkCorrupt when later group members depend on it, otherwise ChunkDigestMismatch.

A decode failure (not only digest mismatch) of a Chunk that a later same-group member within max_lookback frames depends on is reclassified PrerequisiteChunkCorrupt, naming the dependency blast radius.
research_needed: Quantify content made unreadable by one corrupt prerequisite under dense/extreme lookback settings.

statement: ChunkGroup structure: every declared group must have prefix-coded members; each group needs at least two members occupying contiguous frame positions; otherwise InvalidGroupReference or InvalidGroupOrdering.
A ChunkGroup's declared max_preceding_bytes must exactly equal the computed maximum sum of preceding members' logical bytes within max_lookback; mismatch is Corrupt/AccessCostMismatch.

Prefix history for bounded-lookback decoding is the last max_lookback group members' plaintext truncated to the final ZSTD_WINDOW_BYTES (1 MiB, codec.rs:24-25); older history is dropped regardless of lookback.
evidence_in_source: code; parameter chosen without cited measurement in slice
research_needed: Measure ratio gain versus window size (1-8 MiB) and decoder memory for grouped similar files.
decision_needed: Is a 1 MiB prefix window the v1 bound for prefix-coded groups?

statement: Region-owned Chunks are derived from each ReconstructionRegion's start_chunk_index and chunk_count over its ContentObject's chunk list; membership is never listed explicitly.
The writer must decode each region representation, invert its transforms and confirm byte-exact equality with the original member Chunk bytes before emitting; failure is RegionMemberDigestMismatch.
evidence_in_source: code; no integration test references RegionMemberDigestMismatch

statement: The set of region-owned frame declarations must equal the set implied by ReconstructionRegion ranges; otherwise UnknownReconstructionRegion.
A Chunk reconstructed by more than one region must yield identical plaintext each time; a conflict is RegionMemberDigestMismatch.

Region reconstruction is refused (PolicyRefused) when representation exceeds 64 MiB, transformed bytes exceed 64 MiB, logical bytes exceed 64 MiB, or chunk_count exceeds 4096 (jpeg_reconstruction.rs:15-21).
research_needed: Distribution of JPEG sizes in target corpora; memory/time of reconstruction at bounds.

statement: Region reconstruction must produce exactly logical_bytes; member boundaries come from region-owned frame logical lengths; every member digest must match and no trailing bytes may remain (ReconstructedLengthMismatch or RegionMemberDigestMismatch).
reconstruct_region_members is the single whole-object reconstruction authority: INDEXED calls it after CHUNK_DATA, STREAM when the region's ContentObject record arrives.

Index handling: absent gives RebuiltAbsent; payload digest mismatch, malformed/noncanonical records or any locator difference give RebuiltInvalid; in all cases the reader uses the locator map rebuilt from CHUNK_DATA and semantics are unchanged.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements SPEC §4.5 L425 (index validated against authority; wrong-index corpus) and docs/format-v0.md L470-475

statement: Index tolerance covers only its payload: a damaged INDEX section header (magic, id, version, flags, reserved bytes, or length overrunning the footer) is a fatal structural error, although the Index is declared non-authoritative and discardable.
evidence_in_source: code only; no test found by grep of crates/*/tests
research_needed: Mutation experiment on Index header bytes; compare with SPEC expectation that INDEX may be ignored entirely.
decision_needed: Should a reader ignore a structurally damaged trailing INDEX section instead of rejecting the archive?

statement: Even a PresentValid Index is never used to locate data by the in-memory reader; it is only compared with the full rebuilt map, so the Index provides no acceleration in this path.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L472 says a present Index 'is used only if' valid; random.rs is the range-access consumer
research_needed: Measure open cost with and without Index in random-access reader (outside slice).

statement: Section header: 'EBS1', section id u16, version u16 (1), flags u32 zero, reserved u32 zero, payload length u64, SHA-256 of payload (32 bytes), 8 reserved zero bytes; payload follows with no padding or alignment.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L240-243; SPEC §4.3 L407

statement: Sections must appear with contiguous ids starting at 1 in canonical order, each once, with version 1 and zero flags/reserved bytes; the required set for the feature schema must be complete, with only a final Index optional.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.1 L2188-2190 (reserved bits must be zero)

statement: A payload digest mismatch in any section other than INDEX is Corrupt/SectionDigestMismatch.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.3 L407 (per-section digest localises damage)

statement: There is no section directory: sections are discovered by walking 64-byte headers from the end of the preamble to the footer, and the footer locates only DESCRIPTOR and MANIFEST_RECORDS.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.4 L415-419 (one unconditional range request locates everything); docs/format-v0.md L58-60
research_needed: Count HTTP range requests needed to locate CHUNK_DATA/Dictionaries/Index in remote reads; evaluate adding a section table to the footer.
decision_needed: Should the v1 footer or Descriptor carry a full section locator table?

statement: Preamble layout: 0 magic; 8 major; 10 minor; 12 length u32; 16/24/32 incompat, ro_compat, compat; 40 SHA-256 of bytes 16..40; 72 layout; 73 role; 74 budget_declared; 75 reserved; 76 window; 84 working set; 92 decode flags; 96 eight budget u64; 160 dedup window; 168 hostility; 176 footer hint; 184-255 reserved.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L225-236; SPEC §4.2 L372-385

statement: INDEXED preambles must declare a zero STREAM dedup window; STREAM preambles must carry a zero footer hint; both are enforced at write and read.

The feature-bitmap checksum (SHA-256 of the 24 bitmap bytes) must match, letting a reader distinguish a corrupt preamble from an unsupported feature; mismatch reuses reason code SectionDigestMismatch.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.2 L377 and §18.3 L2071 (bitmap checksum distinguishes corrupt from unsupported)
evidence_in_source: code; no dedicated test of checksum mismatch found
decision_needed: Should feature-checksum failure have its own reason code rather than SectionDigestMismatch?

statement: Fewer than 8 bytes or a wrong magic is Nonconforming/BadMagic; a correct magic with fewer than 256 bytes is Truncated but reuses reason code TruncatedFooter.
decision_needed: Should truncation inside the preamble have a distinct reason code?

statement: The preamble's self-declared length field must equal 256; otherwise NoncanonicalEncoding.
private-resource-declaration-v1 (0x1000) may be declared only together with encrypted-indexed-v1 (0x20); otherwise Nonconforming.
The layout discriminant must be 1 (INDEXED) or 2 (STREAM); any other value is Unsupported/UnsupportedRequiredFeature.

The preamble role byte must be 1 (Complete); every other role, such as Sidecar or Incremental, is refused with 'only Complete bootstrap archives are supported', and eam::ArchiveRole has only Complete (eam/model.rs:39-42).
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §8.5 L957-963 (roles Complete, Sidecar, Incremental; role participates in LAI); SPEC §4.2 L382
decision_needed: Which archive roles ship in v1, and how are Sidecar/Incremental base references encoded and verified?

statement: budget_declared must be exactly 0 or 1, preamble byte 75 must be zero, and bytes 184-255 must all be zero; otherwise NoncanonicalEncoding.
evidence_in_source: code only; no test found by grep of crates/*/tests

statement: Preamble bytes 168..176 are the 'hostility summary' field and must be zero; the collision/hostility class summary is reserved but not implemented or defined.

statement: ResourceBudget is serialised as eight big-endian u64 values in order: entry_count, total_logical_bytes, max_single_entry_logical_bytes, max_expansion_ratio_milli, chunk_count, max_path_depth, max_metadata_bytes, max_key_derivation_cost.

statement: INDEXED footer: 8-byte footer magic, total length, Descriptor offset/length, Manifest offset/length, actual entry count, actual total logical bytes, SHA-256 of the preamble, and 32 reserved zero bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L290-293; SPEC §4.4 L415

statement: Footer checks: shorter than 384 bytes or missing footer magic is Truncated/TruncatedFooter; declared total longer than actual is Truncated, shorter is Corrupt (IncorrectTotalLength); preamble digest mismatch is FooterBindingMismatch; reserved bytes must be zero.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.4 L420 and §18.3 L2070 (declared total length distinguishes complete/truncated/corrupt)
evidence_in_source: code; native_ecf.rs ECF-F004 (L305-314), truncated case (L402-404), diagnostic_classes_remain_distinguishable; no INDEXED test of FooterBindingMismatch found

statement: Because the footer is found only at EOF, simple truncation removes the footer and yields TruncatedFooter without any declared-length comparison; the 'truncated at N of M bytes' report is only possible when bytes are appended or the footer survives.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.4 L420 claims truncated-at-N reporting; spec audit spec-02-0048 flags same gap
research_needed: Test truncation reporting fidelity on real partial downloads; consider a leading declared length or periodic sync markers.

statement: No appended data, append-in-place or multi-volume split is possible: the footer must be the final 128 bytes and the declared total must equal the exact file length, so any trailing or split bytes fail.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with SPEC §11.4 L1389 (no prefix, suffix or polyglot)
decision_needed: Is multi-volume or append support a v1 non-goal?

statement: Unencrypted INDEXED integrity is per-section payload SHA-256 plus a preamble-bound footer; no digest covers the whole body or section headers (headers are only canonical-checked), unlike the STREAM footer's body digest.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L293-297 (STREAM footer carries STREAM_BODY digest)
research_needed: Security review of unauthenticated INDEXED integrity: can header or section-boundary manipulation change interpretation undetected? Differential fuzzing.
decision_needed: Should the INDEXED footer bind a digest over the section header chain?

statement: Diagnostic mapping helpers: noncanonical is Nonconforming/NoncanonicalEncoding; structure is Corrupt/SectionStructure; integrity failures are Corrupt with specific codes; resource and arithmetic overflow errors are PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit.

Hostile length fields that overflow usize/u64 are classified PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit rather than Corrupt, and the decoder relies on prior checks before direct indexing (plans[&plan_ref], header[..4], groups[&id]); no fuzz harness exists in the repository.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.5 outcome classes
evidence_in_source: code; no fuzz/ directory or fuzz dependency found
research_needed: cargo-fuzz targets for ecf::open and open_stream_with_limits; classification consistency audit of overflow cases.

statement: container.rs has no unit-test module (only a cfg(test) legacy encrypted helper); its behaviour is covered by integration tests in native_ecf.rs, stream_layout.rs, compression_planner.rs, cross_file_compression.rs, reconstructive_transform.rs, jpeg_whole_object.rs, cdc_dedup.rs and crypto_v1.rs.

No integration test found for INDEXED FooterBindingMismatch, footer-hint mismatch, non-zero hostility/reserved preamble bytes, feature-checksum mismatch, LookbackViolation, RegionMemberDigestMismatch, Index header damage, peek_layout or verify_with_limits.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §19.3 L2123-2131 (versioned conformance corpus with stable IDs)

research_needed: Extend generated conformance corpus with these cases and an observed-outcome matrix.

statement: Generated native conformance corpus ECF-F001..F015 covers bad magic, unsupported version, unknown required feature, incorrect total length, malformed record length, out-of-order/duplicate/unknown fields, section digest, chunk digest, LAI/PCR/AUX and Entry identity/aux mismatches, plus truncation and misleading Index.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §19.3 L2123-2126 (stable case IDs); corpus lives in a test file, not a released artifact (SPEC §19.3 L2131)
decision_needed: Will the ECF-F* cases be exported as a versioned, released corpus with expectation classes?

statement: Record type registry in ECF: 1 Descriptor, 2 TransformPlan, 3 Entry, 4 ContentObject, 5 Fidelity, 6 IndexEntry, 7 PathComponent, 8 MetadataItem, 9 Timestamp, 10 FidelityIssue, 11 Dictionary, 12 ChunkGroup, 13/15/17 TransformStep v1/v2/v3, 14 ReconstructionData, 16 Fallback, 18 Region, 19 Audit v2, 28-36 conversion/preservation, 37-43 platform metadata; 20-27 belong to crypto (crypto/wire.rs:14-21).
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md §Canonical records L301-345

statement: Descriptor v1 carries namespace, identity profile, digest algorithm, planner ID, chunker ID, LAI, PCR, AUX (tags 1-8); v2 adds decode window, working set, flags and the eight budget fields (tags 9-19).
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L305-306

statement: DESCRIPTOR payload must be exactly one type-1 record of version 1 or 2 with exactly the tags of that version, and must re-encode byte-identically; other versions are NoncanonicalEncoding.
Descriptor v1, Descriptor v2 and a maximum-value v2 record are pinned to exact hex bytes and SHA-256 values in docs/descriptor-vectors-v1.txt; the test asserts Descriptor v1 is frozen.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/descriptor-vectors-v1.txt; docs/format-v0.md L459-463

statement: TRANSFORM_PLANS contains only TransformPlan records strictly ordered by plan_id with required tags 1-5,7-9 and optional dictionary tag 6; decoded plans pass codec registry validation and must re-encode byte-identically.
Without codec-transform-v1, a non-empty TransformPlan transform sequence is refused (UnknownTransform) because legacy transform-string placeholders were never operational; they are not reinterpreted.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L347-350

statement: A v1 TransformStep (type 13) cannot carry a reconstruction reference; writing one requires reconstructive-transform-v1 and the v2 step record.

TransformStep v2 (type 15) and v3 (type 17) share fields transform id, parameters and optional reconstruction reference (tag 3); a step record of the wrong type for the schema is rejected rather than reinterpreted.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L351-362

statement: RECONSTRUCTION_DATA holds type-14 records uniquely ordered by reconstruction id, followed only by type-16 fallback records unique per Chunk; each ReconstructionData is validated (reconstruction::validate_data) and the section must re-encode byte-identically.
ReconstructionFallback reasons are a closed enum: 1 unrecognised-or-verification-failed, 2 complete-cost-did-not-win; fallbacks are non-authoritative creation-audit data.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L355-358

statement: RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS holds type-18 region records (13 required tags, unique region id) before type-19 audit records (unique target); interleaving is noncanonical and the section must re-encode byte-identically.

Reconstruction audit targets are Chunk(1), ContentObject(2), Region(3); reasons are NotRecognized(1), Unsupported(2), ExactVerificationFailed(3), CompleteCostDidNotWin(4), RegionDedupConflict(5), ResourcePolicyExcluded(6).
DICTIONARIES holds Dictionary records (id, codec, format, construction string, exact bytes) uniquely ordered by dictionary id, each registry-validated; duplicates are DuplicateSemanticDeclaration.
ChunkGroup records carry only group id, max_lookback (u32) and max_preceding_bytes (u64), uniquely ordered by id; group membership is never listed and is carried solely by frame group_ref.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L280-283

statement: MANIFEST_RECORDS contains all Entry records (canonical LogicalPath order via EntrySet::from_canonical) followed by ContentObject records strictly ordered by logical digest; any other ordering or record type is noncanonical, and the payload must re-encode byte-identically.
The unencrypted manifest is a flat uncompressed sequence of canonical records; there is no compact-manifest encoding, manifest compression or record offset table.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.9 L478 (manifest uncompressed by default; compact-manifest incompat feature for millions of entries)
research_needed: Measure manifest size and open time at 1M-10M entries; decide whether compact-manifest is needed for v1.

statement: STREAM emits each Entry or ContentObject as an individual MANIFEST_RECORD item whose bytes equal that object's slice of the INDEXED MANIFEST_RECORDS payload; the item must hold exactly one canonical record.
ContentObject record carries logical digest, chunk_root and an ordered sequence of 32-byte Chunk ids only, with no per-reference logical offsets or stored sizes.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §13.2 L1519 (chunk table in compressed and logical coordinates)
research_needed: Cost of deriving logical offsets from frame headers for byte-range reads in large files.

statement: Canonical sequences decode only up to 1,000,000 items but the encoder does not enforce that cap, so a ContentObject with over 1M Chunk references (about 122 GiB at the EXTREME 128 KiB target) could be written yet refused on read.
research_needed: Construct a >1M-reference ContentObject via eam types, encode and open; measure manifest sizes for very large files.
decision_needed: Enforce the cap at write, raise it, or make it caller policy?

statement: Entry record version is chosen automatically: version 3 if the Entry is a ReparsePoint or uses platform/security metadata, version 2 if it is a symlink or uses POSIX metadata, otherwise the unchanged version-1 form.
Entry and MetadataItem records use versions 2 and 3, contradicting docs/format-v0.md, which states the only assigned version-2 record is Descriptor type 1.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts docs/format-v0.md §Decisions L31-33
decision_needed: Update format-v0.md record-version statement to reflect Entry/MetadataItem v2/v3?

statement: Entry v1, Entry v2, Entry v2 symlink, ACL v1, Windows security descriptor v1, metadata v3 Windows attributes and Entry v3 reparse records are pinned to hex/SHA-256 vectors in docs/posix-metadata-v1-vectors.txt and docs/security-metadata-v1-vectors.txt.
A ReparsePoint Entry (kind 4) exists only in Entry-v3; encoding or decoding it under a lower version is refused.

Entry v1 represents only Directory (kind 1, content kind 0) and File with internal content (kind 2, content kind 1); a directory with content is DirectoryHasContent, a file without is FileMissingContent, anything else UnsupportedEntryKind.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L308

statement: Symlink and reparse-point cases in the Entry v1 encoder are unreachable!() arms; they cannot panic because Entry::uses_posix_v1 and uses_platform_security_v1 (eam/model.rs:1538-1546) force v2/v3 for those kinds.

Entry v2/v3 field cardinality is closed per kind (directory: none; file: content digest; symlink: encoding and target; reparse: v3 payload); v2 must actually use a symlink or POSIX metadata and v3 a reparse or platform/security metadata, preventing gratuitous version bumps.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.1 L2180 (feature active only when it changes layout)

statement: The Entry wire form has no kinds for device nodes, FIFOs, sockets or whiteouts, and no hard-link entry kind (hard links are a PosixHardlinkGroup metadata item).
decision_needed: Are device/FIFO/socket entries a v1 non-goal or capture-only metadata reported via FidelityReport?

statement: ContentRef in the wire form is only Internal (content digest in this archive); there is no External content reference, so Sidecar/Incremental content cannot be encoded.
Symlink target encodings are 1 (UTF-8) and 2 (POSIX bytes); an unknown encoding is Unsupported/UnsupportedRequiredFeature.

PathComponent encoding supports only UTF-8 (value 1); non-UTF-8 path bytes (POSIX raw names, unpaired UTF-16 surrogates) cannot be represented and decode is refused with 'bootstrap paths require UTF-8'.
research_needed: Frequency of non-UTF-8 names in real Linux/Windows trees and legacy archives.
decision_needed: Does v1 add a raw-bytes or WTF-8 path encoding, or refuse/record non-UTF-8 names as fidelity loss?

statement: Closed metadata name registry IDs: 1 core.executable, 2 core.mtime, 3 posix.mode, 4 uid, 5 gid, 6 hardlink group, 7 xattrs, 8 sparse map, 9 security ACLs, 10 Windows security descriptor, 11 Windows attributes, 12 Windows creation time, 13 Windows reparse original, 14 macOS flags, 15 macOS birthtime.
refines_or_supersedes: Differs from SPEC §20.3 L2207 (open reverse-DNS x- namespace; posix.uname/gname in identity/strict-v1)

statement: There is no open or vendor (x-) metadata namespace and no unknown-item carriage: any name id outside 1-15 or wrong value type is rejected as noncanonical.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.3 L2207 (x- names open, reverse-DNS)
decision_needed: Will v1 carry unknown/vendor metadata items, and with what criticality and safe-to-copy rules?

statement: MetadataItem v1 may encode only core.executable and core.mtime; v2 cannot encode platform/security names; the nested MetadataItem record version must equal the enclosing Entry version.
evidence_in_source: code; records.rs L2741-2750 mixed nested version case

statement: Metadata criticality must be Optional (0) in every record version; a Critical item is refused on decode and no constructor creates one, so criticality-driven fail-closed metadata is not implemented.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.1 L2182-2184 (every metadata item carries a criticality bit)
evidence_in_source: code; grep finds Criticality::Critical only in encoders (records.rs:1329, identity.rs:853)
decision_needed: What does Critical mean for v1 readers and which registered names default to Critical?

statement: MetadataItem records carry name, criticality and restorability only; there is no safe-to-copy bit governing whether rewriting tools may retain unknown items.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.1 L2186 (safe-to-copy bit adopted)

statement: Restorability is fixed by the closed registry: v1/v2 items must be Restorable (1); v3 items must declare exactly the registry's Restorable (1) or CaptureOnly (2) value.
evidence_in_source: code; records.rs L2855-2870 wrong restorability case

statement: posix.mode stores only permission, setuid/setgid and sticky bits (mask 0o7777); file-type or higher bits are noncanonical.
Ownership is numeric only: uid and gid are u32 values with no user/group name fields and no 64-bit ids.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.3 L2207 identity/strict-v1 lists posix.uname and posix.gname
decision_needed: Are posix.uname/gname registered metadata names in v1?

statement: Xattrs are stored as exact name/value byte pairs (XAttrV1, type 37) inside a sequence; sparse maps store logical size plus ordered offset/length extents (types 38/39) validated by SparseMap::new.

ACLs: dialect POSIX.1e(1) or NFSv4(2), scope access(1) or default(2), entries typed allow/deny/audit/alarm with principal forms user_obj, user(uid), group_obj, group(gid), mask, other, OWNER@, GROUP@, EVERYONE@, UUID(16 bytes), plus u32 permissions and flags.
ACL principals are numeric ids or UUIDs only; NFSv4 name-based principals (user@domain strings) and portable name mapping are not representable.
Windows security descriptors are stored as exact validated self-relative bytes (type 42) and reparse points as nonzero u32 tag plus bounded data (type 43).
Timestamp record: signed i64 seconds, u32 nanoseconds, source precision (1 second, 2 centisecond, 3 microsecond, 4 100-nanosecond, 5 nanosecond) and a restorable flag.

FidelityReport record holds captured names, unavailable and degraded issue lists (class, reason, optional entry-scope path), a platform string and filesystem declarations; string and issue sets must be uniquely sorted and byte-canonical.
FidelityReport class, reason, platform and filesystem fields are free-form UTF-8 strings validated only for ordering; no closed registry of fidelity classes or reasons exists at the wire level.
decision_needed: Should fidelity classes/reasons be registry-controlled identifiers for machine consumers?

statement: ConversionProvenance (type 28, version 1 only) records source format, adapter id, source SHA-256, import mode, source entry and observation counts, four conflict-class counts, ordered resolutions, sorted synthesized ancestors, sorted unsupported metadata names and outcome string.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L329

statement: Conversion conflict classes are the closed set omission, refinement, divergence, irreconcilable; each declared class count must be at least the number of resolution records of that class.

Conversion source_format, adapter_id, import_mode, outcome, semantic_field and action are unregistered free-form strings; declared counts may exceed recorded resolutions, so unresolved conflicts are counted but not itemised.
decision_needed: Which conversion-record strings become closed registries, and must every counted conflict carry a resolution record?

statement: LegacyPreservation decoding accepts only preservation_format 'legacy-preservation/v1' with source_format 'ZIP'; exact-source preservation for tar, 7z or other adapters is rejected as noncanonical.
decision_needed: Which adapters must support --preserve exact-source evidence in v1?

statement: LegacyPreservation requires observations ordered by (scope, subject ordinal, observation ordinal), conflicts ordered by ordinal, sorted selected resolutions, SHA-256(source_bytes) equal to source_digest, and byte-canonical re-encoding.

LegacyPreservation embeds the complete exact legacy source bytes in a single record field inside FIDELITY, bypassing chunking, deduplication and compression, so a preserved archive roughly adds the full source size.
research_needed: Measure preserved-archive size versus source and versus storing the source as a chunked ContentObject.
decision_needed: Should preserved source bytes be stored through the ContentStore instead of an inline record?

statement: Preserved LOM evidence records: observation (scope, ordinals, field, authority, raw value, optional interpreted value, evidence location, validity valid/invalid/uninterpreted), conflict, authority (format, structure, instance), typed value (bytes/unsigned/signed/text/boolean), location (offset, length), resolution (action, optional authority).
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L331-337

statement: Conversion string lists use an ad-hoc count-plus-length encoding inside Bytes fields instead of the canonical Sequence field type; the decoder caps preallocation at 1M items and rejects trailing bytes or invalid UTF-8.
decision_needed: Should nested string lists use the canonical Sequence type for a uniform grammar?

statement: Index entry record (type 6) holds Chunk digest, absolute frame offset and stored length; entries must be strictly ordered by Chunk id; each entry is 100 bytes (matching chunker.rs:21).

The chunker's per-unique-Chunk cost model charges a 64-byte frame plus 100-byte Index entry, but archives with cross-file-compression-v1 emit 96-byte frame headers, so chunk-size and dedup decisions may understate per-Chunk overhead by 32 bytes.
research_needed: Compare modelled versus actual container size across profiles; check whether chunk parameter selection changes with the 96-byte cost.

statement: Generated record-level conformance IDs: ECF-REGION-VALID/DUPLICATE/AUDIT-DUPLICATE-001, ECF-RECONSTRUCTION-DUPLICATE/DIGEST/FALLBACK-DUPLICATE-001, ECF-TRANSFORM-UNKNOWN/PARAMETERS/DUPLICATE-001 and ECF-CODEC-UNKNOWN-001, each asserting a typed reason code.
Archive codec strings cannot select unregistered code: an unknown codec id is UnknownCodec, and repeating a transform family within one plan is DuplicateSemanticDeclaration.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §20.1 L2192; SPEC §5.8 registry
evidence_in_source: unit test ECF-CODEC-UNKNOWN-001, ECF-TRANSFORM-DUPLICATE-001; compression_planner.rs unknown codec (L328-337)

statement: A sequential reader learns a Chunk's destination only after its later manifest record, so decoded plaintext is staged in a bounded resident set that spills to a private temporary file; the no-Seek guarantee applies to the archive source, not this scratch file.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/stream-layout-v1.md (records after data)

statement: StagingLimits has memory_bytes (resident plaintext before spilling) and total_bytes (all staged plaintext); memory_only(n) sets both equal so no temporary file is ever created.

Staging insert ignores already-staged Chunk ids, spills oldest resident entries first-in-first-out until the new plaintext fits, and writes a plaintext larger than the memory limit directly to the spill file.

total_bytes is cumulative: staged_bytes is incremented before the limit check and never decremented on release, and released spill bytes are not reclaimed until drop, so the limit bounds bytes ever staged per pass (default 64 GiB, stream.rs:340-345), not concurrent usage.
research_needed: Measure temp-file growth and false refusals on long STREAM archives with late manifest records.
decision_needed: Should total_bytes bound concurrent staged bytes with spill-space reuse?

statement: Spilled plaintext is written unencrypted to std::env::temp_dir() using default OS permissions and a pid/counter/nanosecond name with create_new; deletion happens only in Drop, so a crash or kill leaves decoded plaintext on disk.
evidence_in_source: code; stream_layout.rs::staging_spills_within_its_memory_bound_and_leaves_nothing_behind covers normal and truncated failure (L639-684), not crashes
research_needed: Security review for multi-user hosts and future encrypted STREAM; test cleanup on abort/panic.
decision_needed: Should spill files be restricted-permission, encrypted with an ephemeral key, or placed in a caller-chosen directory?

statement: The staging directory is not configurable: spill files always go to the system temporary directory, with up to 64 unique-name attempts before failing with PolicyRefused/Io.
Staged reads return a copy of resident plaintext or seek-and-read the spill file; a Chunk no longer staged is Nonconforming/UnknownChunk.
Releasing a resident Chunk scans the FIFO queue linearly and every read clones plaintext, so staging cost may grow with retained Chunk count and Chunk size; no benchmark is present.
research_needed: Benchmark STREAM unpack with 1e5-1e6 retained Chunks.

statement: Staging exposes peak resident bytes, spilled bytes and retained Chunk count; the STREAM report surfaces peak_resident_staging_bytes and spilled_staging_bytes (stream.rs:296-297).
Staging I/O failures are classified PolicyRefused/Io and arithmetic overflows PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit, never Corrupt, since they concern the reader's environment rather than the archive.
The spill file is created with create_new, is never reachable through a caller-supplied path, and is removed when the store is dropped, including after failure or truncation.
The unencrypted native containers now encode symlink and Windows reparse-point Entries, contradicting docs/format-v0.md, which says both layouts carry only directory and regular-file entries.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts docs/format-v0.md §Container L40-41
decision_needed: Update format-v0.md container scope statement?

statement: The container serialises no Merkle outboard or verification tree; verified partial reads can use only per-Chunk digests (frame chunk_id) and ContentObject chunk_root, not a Merkle slice bound to signed PCR.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §8.6 L975-977 and §13.2 L1527 (Merkle slice for verified partial reads)
research_needed: Evaluate whether flat chunk digests plus ContentObject chunk list suffice for remote partial verification under signature.
decision_needed: Is MERKLE_OUTBOARD required in v1?

statement: No padding, alignment or size-hiding exists in unencrypted section or Chunk framing; payloads are contiguous and every Chunk's stored size is visible in its frame header.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.3 L407 (no padding); crypto padding handled in crypto layer

statement: The ECF declarations define no media type or file-extension constant; the .eb extension is hardcoded in archive/filesystem.rs:434 and CLI code, and application/vnd.entrybound.archive appears nowhere.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §18.1 L2023-2036 (.eb, .eba fallback); SPEC §18.2 L2040-2042 (application/vnd.entrybound.archive)
evidence_in_source: grep of crates for extension/media type strings
decision_needed: Freeze .eb versus .eba and register the vendor media type before v1?

statement: INDEXED serialisation is deterministic: identical EAM input produces identical bytes and identities, since all ordering, reserved fields and derived declarations are canonical and no timestamps or random values are written.
research_needed: Cross-platform and cross-version byte-equality checks in CI.

statement: Rechunking or adding/removing the Index changes PCR or PCI respectively while LAI and AUX stay fixed; the container binds neither layout nor frame order into logical identities.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md §Layout equivalence L409-416

statement: The encrypted re-entry path hardcodes layout INDEXED, role Complete and dedup window 0 for the authenticated descriptor; no encrypted STREAM construction exists in the container code.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L43-44, L432 (encrypted STREAM deferred and must fail closed)
decision_needed: Is encrypted STREAM (pipe-friendly encrypted archives) required for v1?

statement: DecodeRequirements flags (u32 at preamble 92..96) are only checked as a subset of caller-permitted flags; no flag bits are defined and every current plan and policy uses 0.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §4.2 L379 (DecodeRequirements declares whether any feature needs an unusual decoder capability)
evidence_in_source: code; grep shows flags: 0 in codec.rs:229, 270, 1092 and archive.rs:57
decision_needed: Which decoder capability flags exist in v1 (e.g. large-window, float-dependent, reconstruction working set)?
